findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for Cisco UCS assigns all collected data the sourcetype cisco:ucs and sets source to cisco:ucs:<classId> (for example cisco:ucs:equipmentPsuStats); collection is configured with templates of classIds attached to a Cisco UCS input, not a separate 'Cisco UCS statistics' input. The same false sourcetype appears in dataSources, implementation and exclusions.
findings.quote: keep the add-on’s default sourcetype for statistics, which is `cisco:ucs:stats` — this is the only sourcetype this UC targets.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe creating a template with the environmental classIds (equipmentPsuStats, equipmentChassisStats, processorEnvStats, computeMbTempStats, ...) and attaching it to a Cisco UCS input; search sourcetype=cisco:ucs with source=cisco:ucs:<classId>, or document the custom sourcetype if one is set on the input.

findings.explanation: For every thermal and watt row the two numbers sit in the crit_low and crit_high columns, so the SPL treats any reading below 33 C (or below 900 W per PSU, below 80 C per CPU socket, etc.) as Critical. A reader pasting this 'literal copy' CSV gets a fleet of red rows for healthy hardware, contradicting the note that 'thermals and watts use high-side warn/crit'.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the values to warn_high/crit_high for thermal and power rows (for example `equipmentChassisStats,chassis_ambient,,33,,40,C,...`), keep low-side columns for fans and the 12 V rail, and correct the row count (13 rows, not 12).

findings.explanation: The SPL groups `stats ... by dn, classId, metric, chassis_num, fi_side`; stats drops events whose BY fields are null, so chassis rows (no fi_side) and FI rows (no chassis_num) are both removed. The troubleshooting text promises rows the search can never return.
findings.quote: `chassis_num` is empty on some DNs — expected for some FI-only or IOM paths; the dn is still valid. Do not filter those rows out
findings.suggested_fix: Once the SPL is fixed (fillnull on chassis_num/fi_side before stats), keep this note; until then state that rows without both fields are excluded.

findings.explanation: The attribute mapping is guessed (long coalesce lists such as ambientTemp/frontTemp on equipmentChassisStats, a '12V rail' on computeMbPowerStats). In the UCSM object model computeMbPowerStats reports consumed power and input voltage/current and computeMbTempStats uses fmTempSen* attributes, and stats DNs do not contain 'front'/'rear', so the mb_temp_front/rear branches may never match.
findings.quote: Power, cooling, and fan readings appear as statistics events for `equipmentChassisStats`, ... `computeMbTempStats`, `computeMbPowerStats`
findings.suggested_fix: Check the UCS Manager XML API object reference for each class and list the real attribute names (for example equipmentChassisStats inputPower/outputPower, computeMbPowerStats consumedPower/inputVoltage); rename the rail_12v metric accordingly.

findings.explanation: The SPL computes no count and has no -24h threshold; it takes the latest value per sensor and rates it against warn/crit bounds from ucs_environmental_thresholds. The description never says what makes a row Critical or Warn.
findings.suggested_fix: Say: latest reading per sensor dn over 24 h (chassis/PSU power, PSU/CPU/board/IOM temperatures, fan RPM) compared with per-class bounds in ucs_environmental_thresholds; Critical/Warn when outside crit/warn bounds, NoBaseline when no lookup row exists.

findings.explanation: The title names a specific API reference but the URL is the cisco.com home page.
findings.quote:
"title": "Cisco UCS Manager XML API Reference, Release 4.2 (MO and statistics model)",
      "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the UCS Manager XML API Programmer's Guide / object model reference for the release in scope, and add the add-on's Sources page (splunk.github.io/splunk-add-on-for-cisco-ucs/Sources/).

findings.explanation: Marked verified while the sourcetype, lookup and BY-clause problems mean the search returns nothing or false Criticals on a standard install.
findings.suggested_fix: Set to draft until validated against real Splunk_TA_cisco_ucs data.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: All three searches filter sourcetype="cisco:ucs:stats", which the add-on does not emit (it uses sourcetype cisco:ucs with source cisco:ucs:<classId>), so a default install returns no rows.

`stats latest(_time) ... by dn, classId, metric, chassis_num, fi_side` discards any result where a BY field is null; chassis/blade DNs never contain switch-A|B and FI DNs never contain chassis-N, so almost every row is dropped. Add `fillnull value="-" chassis_num fi_side` before stats (rex max_match=0 also makes these multivalue; drop max_match=0).

summary: The implementation walk-through is detailed and specific to UCS environmental MOs, but it hard-codes a 'cisco:ucs:stats' sourcetype and 'statistics modular input' the add-on does not have, the shipped threshold CSV puts the high-side limits in the crit_low column so normal readings rate Critical, and the SPL's stats BY clause drops every row lacking chassis_num or fi_side. Description, value, KFP and controlTest are template residue.
